decisions.reason: The message reports that the implemented second V lost its already-required subtle right-arm reach; the candidate's requirement value remains unchanged and the same-message runtime failure already records the implementation mismatch.
Requiring the E and L forms to follow the Hero V's architectural language does not modify the approved Hero V geometry.
The peak-alignment requirement is independently introduced by the same message and already has a complete matching Event; the E/L letterform modification adds nothing to it.
Avoiding Roman-style flared terminals on the E and L does not change the existing shared signature-terminal rule for the Hero V, second V, and É accent.
The source preserves the existing literal Hero V terminal derivation and separately introduces peak alignment; the E/L modification does not alter the derivation requirement.
The E/L geometry and terminal refinement does not resume or modify the deferred champagne material treatment.
Although the message evaluates the full wordmark, it does not change the existing kerning or unified-reading requirement.
The request to restore the second V's right-arm reach concerns glyph geometry, not its relative visual prominence or height hierarchy.
The source provides design feedback but does not change the obligation to include rationale with review rounds.
The E/L letterform decision has no effect on acceptable proof attachment formats.
